analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The patch excerpt documents a new `darkbloom update --rollback` flag with `--yes`, and the quarantine-override wording. The visible units are base text (lines 2135-2374, 2375-2519) and head text (lines 1-385) of the same file. Neither has any code or runtime-config change in the supplied evidence, so no control is weakened here and no finding is raised.

Security-relevant claims in the doc excerpt:
- Rollback restores the retained predecessor and quarantines the installed release.
- It runs the watchdog's journaled rollback under the update lease, and drains the provider first unless `--force` is used.
- It contacts no coordinator, and `--rollback` cannot be combined with `--check-only`, `--override-quarantine` or `--coordinator`.
- The documented flow includes a confirmation prompt, and `--yes` is required when stdin is not a terminal.

This touches the T-043 area (rollback authority is the same replaceable provider binary, TB-003) and the update/quarantine path. The implementing code (provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/UpdateRollback.swift and the watchdog journaled rollback) is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify the following:
- Whether the restored predecessor is re-verified against the coordinator's release/binary-hash registry (A-011).
- Whether App Attest build qualification or revocation (A-017, T-054) is rechecked after a rollback.
- Whether a revoked or vulnerable predecessor can be reinstalled by a local operator, which is a downgrade concern for T-047-style staleness.

The rest of the supplied head text (lines 1-385) and base text (lines 2135-2519) contain no changed lines per the patch ranges (changed head ranges are 743-769, 1852 and 1859-1860). They are pre-existing documentation of the CLI, paths, env passthrough, the add-on socket and sandbox paths (TB-012/TB-013), and the cache (T-041), and are not new regressions. The doc's statement that the rollback restores a retained predecessor needs checking against the implementation in a later pass, but no concrete regression is shown here.
